claim: Vertical scaling (scaling up) adds more power to existing infrastructure, such as more CPU or memory for an instance; you resize an EC2 instance by changing its instance type, and you then pay the rate of the new instance type.

evidence.quote: As your needs change, you might find that your Amazon EC2 instance is too big or too small for its workload. If this is the case, you can resize your instance by changing its instance type.
evidence.title: Amazon EC2 instance type changes

evidence.quote: When you change the instance type, you'll start paying the rate of the new instance type.
evidence.title: Amazon EC2 instance type changes
Choosing an AWS compute service
evidence.quote: The scalability of a service can be **vertical**, allowing you to scale up by adding more power to your existing infrastructure (like increasing the CPU or memory of an instance), or **horizontal**, helping you to scale out by adding more instances to handle the load.
